label: JZ Mock C · Paper 2 · Question 18
knowledgePattern: Convert a gradient condition into a bounded plane region
solution:
f′(q)=3q2−2pq−p2=(3q+p)(q−p). The allowed region in the square [−3,3]×[−3,3] therefore satisfies this product being nonnegative.

The boundary lines are q=p and q=−p/3. For p > 0 the product is negative between the lines; for p < 0 it is again negative between their lower and upper values.

The two excluded triangular wedges each have horizontal height 3 and vertical base 4, so each has area 6. Subtracting them from the square of area 36 gives 24. The boundary lines have zero area and are included by the non-strict inequality. Answer C.

hints.recap: Parameters are held constant when differentiating with respect to the input.
hints.pitfall: The vertical constant does not affect gradient.

hints.title: Draw and test the boundary regions
hints.body: Replace each factor by zero to find boundary lines in the parameter plane. Intersect their sign regions with the stated square.
hints.recap: Draw boundary lines, test a point in each region and retain the portions satisfying all restrictions.
hints.pitfall: A product is nonnegative when its factors have matching signs; the lines alone are not the whole region.
